video.title: Meet Abdulkaiz: how I design and build

story:
Most people who build things for the web stop at either design or code. I never got comfortable with that split, so I learned both.

I put my first project on the internet in 2016 and never really stopped. My best-known piece of open source is Bibata — a cursor theme I designed and built that ended up shipping as a default on Linux distributions I'd never met the maintainers of. It's been downloaded more than 1.4 million times, which still surprises me.

That's the same job I do for clients: take something small and fiddly, design it properly, and build it so it holds up on a stranger's machine.
bio:
I'm a design engineer based in Bhuj, India. I work in the overlap between design and front-end development — usually starting in Figma and finishing in Webflow, WordPress, Framer or plain code, depending on what the project actually needs.

The open-source work is the part I'm proudest of. Alongside Bibata I maintain github-nvim-theme, apple_cursor and clickgen, a Python toolbox for building cursor themes. Between them that's a few thousand stars and a lot of strangers trusting my work on their own machines, which is a strange and lovely thing to think about.

On Upwork I'm Top Rated with a 98% job success score across 45 five-star reviews. Most of that work is the same thing I do here: taking a design from a Figma file to a live, fast site.

I care about the details you only notice when they're missing — load times, empty states, error messages, and what happens on a slow phone. I work directly with founders and small teams: clear scope, steady updates, and something that's fast by default.
